tokensave is a code-graph MCP server. Start with tokensave_context for any code exploration task — it returns relevant symbols, relationships, and code snippets for a natural-language query. Use tokensave_search to find specific symbols by name. Discovery and analysis tools are read-only and safe to call in parallel. Edit and session-memory tools can mutate local project state and declare readOnlyHint=false. [open] Issue #290: [see-something] tests: ConsentGateTests is a permanent compile-RED that makes Record-Foundation untestable (Record-Foundation/Tests/Unit/Domain/ConsentGateTests.swift)
  Author: @sam-fakhreddine
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/gitrdunhq/Record-Suite/issues/290

  Description:
    `Record-Foundation/Tests/Unit/Domain/ConsentGateTests.swift` is a T1.1 'RED trigger' test referencing a `ConsentGate` protocol that was never implemented (zero hits outside the test file). Because Swift builds *all* test targets for any `swift test` invocation, this one file breaks compilation of every test target in the Record-Foundation package — no Foundation test has been runnable standalone since the monorepo consolidation (9a283cc7).
    
    Nobody noticed because the root package's test run doesn't include sub-package test targets.
    
    **What's wrong:** a compile-failing RED test parked in-tree defeats the purpose of a test target; RED gates should block a task branch, not main.
    
    **Interim fix (landed in the #280 branch):** the file is `exclude:`d from the `DomainTests` target with a comment pointing here, so `UtilitiesTests` (new in #280) can run.
    
    **Real fix options:** implement ConsentGate and un-exclude, or delete the test if T1.1 is abandoned.
----
[open] Issue #293: [see-something] test: stale source assertion — MCPLifecycleTests still expects server.stop() removed in #249 (Record-ML/Tests/Unit/MCPLifecycleTests.swift:66)
  Author: @sam-fakhreddine
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/gitrdunhq/Record-Suite/issues/293

  Description:
    **What's wrong:** `MCPLifecycleTests.appAssemblerHasTeardown` asserts `source.contains("server.stop()")` against AppAssembler.swift, but commit c45ff579 (#249, DuckDBCommandServer removal) deleted the assembler's `server.stop()` wiring without updating this test. The test has been red on main since that commit.
    
    **Why it matters:** a permanently-failing suite normalizes red CI — the next real regression in this file gets ignored. (Sibling to the pre-existing failures tracked in #289.)
    
    **Suggested fix:** drop the `server.stop()` expectation (the server no longer exists) and keep the `func teardown()` assertion, or replace it with an assertion matching the current #280 teardown shape (`withAsyncTeardown` + `storage?.close()`).
    
    Found while running the Record-ML suite for #279.
----
[open] Issue #294: [see-something] test: localization lint red on main — OnboardingView .accessibilityLabel("Onboarding") hardcoded literal (Record-Foundation/Tests LocalizationInfrastructureTests.swift:181)
  Author: @sam-fakhreddine
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/gitrdunhq/Record-Suite/issues/294

  Description:
    **What's wrong:** `task-007 Localization AC-2b` fails on main: `OnboardingView.swift:33` uses `.accessibilityLabel("Onboarding")` as a hardcoded literal, introduced in f759a31a (beta-ga batch) without updating either the view (localized key) or the lint test's allowlist.
    
    **Why it matters:** permanently-red suite in Record-Foundation (749/750) — masks real regressions; sibling of #289/#293.
    
    **Suggested fix:** localize the label (`String(localized:)` / catalog key) — it's user-facing via VoiceOver — or, if intentionally unlocalized, add it to the test's exemption list with a comment.

# THE RECORD

Local-first macOS meeting transcription app. Swift 6.2, Clean Architecture, TDD.

## Resume

Read `CURRENT_STATE.md` — it has the current epic, phase, and next action.

## Orchestration

This file is the conductor. Epics execute in dependency order:

```
COMPLETED                                    REMAINING
─────────                                    ─────────
Epic 1: Core Recording ─┐
Epic 1.5: Capture Fixes  ├──→ Epic 3.5: Parakeet + Telemetry (no UI)
Epic 3: Transcription    │
Epic 4: Diarization     ─┘──→ Epic 5: Menu Bar UI (needs desk)
Epic 2: Storage         ─┘──→ Epic 6: Summarization (MLX/GPU)
                              Epic 7: Streaming + Translation
                              Epic 8: THE RECORD Engine (MCP + NLP)
```

Each epic follows 5 phases: **REFINE** (SPEC) → **PLAN** (TASKS.md) → **PROPERTIES** (formal properties) → **ACT** (code) → **VALIDATE** (integration).
Human checkpoint after PLAN and before ACT. Within ACT, layers build sequentially: Domain → Business → Infrastructure → Presentation.

PROPERTIES.md (template at `docs/planning/PROPERTIES-TEMPLATE.md`) captures 11 property categories:
FUNCTIONAL, SAFETY, LIVENESS, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, RELIABILITY, CONCURRENCY, OBSERVABILITY, UX, DATA INTEGRITY, PRIVACY.
Each property drives test generation (RED briefs) and reviewer validation (traceability matrix).

## Skills (Progressive Disclosure)

Read the skill file when entering that phase. Don't load all skills upfront.

| Phase / Layer | Skill File to Read |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Full epic workflow | `.claude/skills/therecord-epic-executor/SKILL.md` |
| Domain types | `.claude/skills/therecord-domain-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Business actors | `.claude/skills/therecord-business-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Infrastructure | `.claude/skills/therecord-infrastructure-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Presentation | `.claude/skills/therecord-presentation-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Quality gate | `.claude/skills/therecord-integration-validator/SKILL.md` |
| Pre-merge bug hunt | `.claude/skills/therecord-bug-hunt/SKILL.md` |

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

**Before any rename swarm, run GitNexus impact analysis to get the complete caller map:**

```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "methodName", direction: "upstream", file_path: "path/to/file.swift", includeTests: true })
```

Pass the full `byDepth.1` list to each rename agent — no grepping, no missed call sites.

**After the swarm, reindex and verify zero orphans:**

```bash
node ~/.npm/_npx/32f98f05d98eef45/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
```

Then run:
```
gitnexus_cypher("MATCH (a)-[{type:'CALLS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'oldName' RETURN a.name, a.filePath")
```

Any remaining hits = confirmed orphaned calls. The DuckDB `.execute()` SQL calls are false positives — filter by `filePath NOT CONTAINS 'DuckDB'` if needed.

## Subagent Briefing

When spawning agents for parallel work, include in the prompt:
- The skill file path to read
- SPEC and PLAN file paths for the current epic
- `Swift 6.2 -strict-concurrency=complete`, file size limits, TDD discipline
- context7 MCP access: `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__query-docs`

## Canonical Decisions (override older docs)

Some architecture docs predate the SPEC-EPIC1 v2.0 research enrichment. When in conflict:
- **Audio capture:** ScreenCaptureKit (NOT CATapDescription). SPEC-EPIC1.md is authoritative.
- **Project name:** THE RECORD (not "Meeting Transcriber Pro"). Some planning docs use the old name.
- **Observation:** @Observable (NOT ObservableObject). macOS 15+ only.

## Single Source of Truth — Canonical Defaults

**Never hardcode a value that already has a named canonical source.** Reference the source directly so changes propagate automatically.

| Value | Canonical source | Wrong |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

PROPERTIES.md (template at `docs/planning/PROPERTIES-TEMPLATE.md`) captures 11 property categories:
FUNCTIONAL, SAFETY, LIVENESS, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, RELIABILITY, CONCURRENCY, OBSERVABILITY, UX, DATA INTEGRITY, PRIVACY.
Each property drives test generation (RED briefs) and reviewer validation (traceability matrix).

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

**Before any rename swarm, run GitNexus impact analysis to get the complete caller map:**

```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "methodName", direction: "upstream", file_path: "path/to/file.swift", includeTests: true })
```

Pass the full `byDepth.1` list to each rename agent — no grepping, no missed call sites.

**After the swarm, reindex and verify zero orphans:**

```bash
node ~/.npm/_npx/32f98f05d98eef45/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
```

Then run:
```
gitnexus_cypher("MATCH (a)-[{type:'CALLS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'oldName' RETURN a.name, a.filePath")
```

Any remaining hits = confirmed orphaned calls. The DuckDB `.execute()` SQL calls are false positives — filter by `filePath NOT CONTAINS 'DuckDB'` if needed.

Some architecture docs predate the SPEC-EPIC1 v2.0 research enrichment. When in conflict:

- **Project name:** THE RECORD (not "Meeting Transcriber Pro"). Some planning docs use the old name.

## Single Source of Truth — Canonical Defaults

**Never hardcode a value that already has a named canonical source.** Reference the source directly so changes propagate automatically.

| Value | Canonical source | Wrong |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY5OTk2NTc=","is_bot":false,"login":"sam-fakhreddine","name":"Sam Fakhreddine"},"body":"## Summary

Full test suite consistently hits the 300s hard timeout when run with `--parallel`. WhisperKitPlugin tests are the slowest individual tests but a hang (not just slow tests) is suspected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `python3 scripts/test.py` (runs `swift test --parallel`)
2. Wait 300 seconds
3. **Observe:** process killed by timeout; no test result summary printed

## Expected Behavior

Test suite completes within 120s (parallel mode should be faster than serial).

## Actual Behavior

Suite hangs past 300s. Slowest reported tests are WhisperKitPlugin-related (~1.5s each), but their total is ~10s — not enough to explain 300s. Likely a test that does not respect cancellation or a resource leak (subprocess, file descriptor) that causes a deadlock in parallel mode.

## Root Cause (suspected)

WhisperKitPlugin tests may launch a subprocess (MCP or ML inference mock) that never terminates when the test is cancelled in parallel mode. Alternatively, a shared resource (DuckDB file lock, temp directory) may deadlock when multiple test processes access it simultaneously.

## Affected Files

- Record-App/scripts/test.py — timeout configuration
- Record-ML/Tests/Unit/WhisperKitPluginTests.swift — slowest tests
- Record-ML/Tests/Unit/MCPSummarizationPluginTests.swift — suspected subprocess leak (see the-record #222)

## Investigation Steps

1. Run serial: `swift test` (no `--parallel`) — does it complete?
2. Run with filter: `swift test --filter WhisperKit` — isolate the slow tests
3. Run without WhisperKit: `swift test --parallel --skip WhisperKit` — does the rest complete?
4. Check for orphaned processes after timeout: `ps aux | grep -E "swift|whisper|mcp"`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Full test suite completes in < 120s with `--parallel`
- [ ] No orphaned subprocesses after test completion
- [ ] No test hangs when cancelled (all tests respect Task.isCancelled)
- [ ] Timeout increased to 600s as interim safety net

## Severity

Medium — CI affected, workaround: run serial

## Summary
11 tests assert the current (incorrect) behavior instead of the desired behavior—they pass when code is wrong and fail when you fix it.

## Location
Record-Presentation/Tests/ (identify via test audit)

## Why It Matters
These tests lock in bugs. When someone fixes the underlying bug, tests fail, signaling the fix is wrong. Developers then revert the fix. The bug becomes permanent.

## Suggested Fix
Audit the 11 tests to identify which ones have inverted assertions. Flip assertions to check for the correct (not current) behavior. For example, if a test expects `isValid == false` when it should be `true`, swap the assertion.

Each test fix should:
1. Confirm the current behavior is indeed a bug (code review or spec review)
2. Flip the assertion to the desired behavior
3. Verify the test fails on the old code, passes on the fix

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 11 tests identified and documented
- [ ] Each test assertion verified against spec/intended behavior
- [ ] Assertions flipped to test the correct behavior
- [ ] All 11 tests fail on the old (buggy) code
- [ ] All 11 tests pass once the bug is fixed
- [ ] No test should flip back without explicit bug report/fix

content.content:
**Audit attempt (2026-07-04, agent-swarm remediation).**

## Finding: the original 11 tests could not be located, and this issue's premise doesn't match current code

The issue body has no list, no comments, and no link to the source audit — it says only "identify via test audit." `git log --all --grep` for "inverted", "#78", and "regression resistance" returns nothing; the enumeration from the predecessor `the-record` repo (issue #78) does not appear to have carried over in any commit, doc, or code comment in this repo.

I searched `Record-Presentation/Tests/` for the actual pattern #134 describes — **a test that currently PASSES while asserting incorrect/buggy behavior, and would FAIL once the underlying bug is fixed** — using:
- keyword sweeps (`known bug`, `current (incorrect)`, `documents current`, `workaround`, `lock in`, `accepted behavior`, etc.)
- manual read-through of every file flagged by those sweeps

**Result: zero matches for a genuinely inverted test.** Every "bug"-flagged test I found is the *opposite* of what #134 describes — a properly-written RED regression test that asserts the *desired* (correct) behavior and is expected to fail until the fix lands, e.g.:

- `RecordingStateOrderingTests.swift:44` — asserts `forceStop()` precedes state reset (correct order), fails today because the code has the bug
- `MenuBarPipelineRaceTests.swift:203,254` (BM-036) — assert stale pipeline results must NOT appear after a new recording starts
- `MenuBarViewModelExportTests.swift:122` (BM-001) — asserts export reaches the engine when the desktop URL guard is fixed
- `RecordingStateDualTrackTests.swift:169` — asserts a `.system`-tagged segment exists; currently fails because code mistags everything as `.microphone`

These are exactly the pattern #134 wants (assert correct behavior, RED until fixed) — they are not bugs in the test suite.

## Recommendation

I could not confirm this issue's core claim against current code. Given zero identifiable false-inverted assertions after a targeted sweep of 75+ test files, options:
1. **Close as unable-to-reproduce** — the original 11 may have already been fixed/flipped in prior remediation waves (this session alone closed 6 issues whose fixes involved these same files), or the migration from `the-record` lost the actionable detail.
2. **Keep open but retitle** to "re-derive the list from the-record#78 if that repo/issue is still accessible" — if the source repo history is available, pulling the original issue body directly (not just the migrated summary) may recover the actual 11 file:line references.

No code changes made — this was a read-only audit per Wave 1c of the remediation plan.

[migrated] test: step-wise ViewModel tests for stop→transcribe→diarize pipeline (the-record #113)
## User Story

As a maintainer, I want integration-style tests that verify the full recording pipeline (stop → transcribe → diarize → summarize) so that I can catch regressions in the handoffs between steps.

## Context

Currently, each plugin is tested in isolation:
- TranscriptionEngine has unit tests that verify a mock audio file is transcribed
- SummarizationEngine has unit tests that verify a mock transcript is summarized
- DiarizationEngine has unit tests that verify speaker labels are assigned

But there are no tests that exercise the sequence: stop recording → transcribe → diarize → summarize → final summary is populated. This leaves handoff bugs (e.g., diarization output format doesn't match summarization input format) undetected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Integration test suite**: New test file `Record-PresentationTests/MenuBarViewModelIntegrationTests.swift`
- [ ] **Full sequence test**: Test verifies: start recording → stop after 5 seconds → transcription completes → diarization completes → summarization completes → final `Recording` object has all fields populated (transcript, speakers, summary)
- [ ] **Mock engines**: Uses in-memory mock engines (not real WhisperKit/MLX) that simulate realistic I/O delays and success/failure scenarios
- [ ] **State snapshots**: Test checks state at each step: `state.isRecording`, `state.transcriptAvailable`, `state.diarizationAvailable`, `state.summaryAvailable`
- [ ] **Error recovery**: Test that if transcription fails, user can retry; if diarization fails, summary can still run
- [ ] **Timeout handling**: Test that if a step exceeds timeout (e.g., transcription takes >60 seconds), the pipeline cancels and reports error
- [ ] **Speaker pairing**: If diarization is enabled, final `Recording.speakers` contains speaker names and turn counts
- [ ] **Coverage**: At least 3 test cases (happy path, transcription failure + retry, diarization timeout)

## Location

`Record-PresentationTests/MenuBarViewModelIntegrationTests.swift` (new file)
`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Features/Recording/MenuBarViewModelEngine.swift` (test target)

## Relates to

#130 (once orchestration is centralized, these tests become straightforward)

[see-something] ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml is entirely commented out — no CI runs on push/PR (ci.yml)
## What's wrong

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has every line commented out — `on:` triggers, both `test-macos`/`test-windows` jobs, everything. The file still exists and is registered as an active workflow, so GitHub triggers a run on every push, immediately reports 0 jobs, and marks the run **failure**. Example: run 28694999720 on PR #283 (fix/72-73-adversarial-reaudit) — completed instantly, `total_count: 0` jobs, conclusion `failure`.

## Why it matters

- Every PR shows a red X in status checks that has nothing to do with the actual change — trains reviewers to ignore/dismiss CI failures, which is how a real failure eventually gets missed.
- No actual test coverage runs in CI at all right now — `swift test`/`scripts/test.py` results only exist because a human or agent ran them locally before pushing.

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Restore the workflow (swap `just test` for whatever the real test entrypoint is now — `scripts/test.py`, not `just`, based on current repo conventions) and get it green, or
2. If CI is intentionally not ready yet, delete/disable the workflow file entirely (or add `if: false` / remove the `on:` triggers cleanly) so pushes don't generate a false-failure status check.

Found while verifying PR #283 (adversarial re-audit of #72/#73) — the failing check on that PR is this pre-existing condition, not a regression from that PR's changes.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test-macos:
    # Self-hosted Mac (mancini) — GitHub-hosted macOS minutes bill at 10x,
    # and the hosted runner checkout leaves LFS-backed Package.swift files
    # (Prebuilts/*) as pointer stubs, which breaks dependency resolution.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
      with:
        lfs: true
    - name: Set up Just
      uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v2.0.0
    - name: Run Tests
      run: just test

  test-windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    # Record-CrossPlatform-Foundation is the only package targeting Windows.
    # It does not currently compile (11 errors, tracked as #287), so this job
    # is manual-only (workflow_dispatch) until that's resolved — running it on
    # every PR just burns paid Windows minutes on a guaranteed failure.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
    - name: Run Tests
      run: swift test --package-path Record-CrossPlatform-Foundation

[see-something] docs/build: Record-Presentation standalone package cannot build — 19 files import Business with no dependency (Record-Presentation/Package.swift:41)
**What's wrong**
`Record-Presentation/Package.swift` carries a TODO ('Presentation imports Business — need to either extract Business as a shared package or stub the dependency') but declares no Business dependency and provides no stub. 19 files under `Record-Presentation/Sources` import Business directly, so the standalone build documented in `Record-Presentation/README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (`git clone && swift build`) is a hard compile break today, not the 'some features will need stubs' soft gap the CONTRIBUTING wording suggests.

**Why it matters**
Anyone following the package's own docs hits an immediate build failure; the sub-package manifest also feeds SourceKit, producing persistent false 'cannot find type' diagnostics for any Presentation type that touches Business (e.g. SpeakerNamingViewModel in #300).

**Suggested fix**
Either (a) extract Business into a shared package the standalone manifest can depend on, (b) add a stub Business target to the standalone Package.swift, or (c) update README/CONTRIBUTING to state plainly that the standalone build is currently broken and the root monorepo Package.swift is the only supported build.

1	# THE RECORD — Presentation Layer
2	
3	The Broadsheet newspaper UI for THE RECORD. SwiftUI views and @Observable ViewModels.
4	
5	This repo is designed for designers and UI developers to work on the interface without needing the full application stack.
6	
7	## Architecture
8	
9	- `ViewModels/` — @MainActor @Observable classes that drive the UI
10	- `Views/` — SwiftUI views organized by feature
11	- `Views/Components/` — Reusable UI components
12	
13	## Requirements
14	
15	- macOS 26+
16	- Xcode 16.3+

# Contributing to THE RECORD

## Monorepo Architecture

THE RECORD is a local-first macOS meeting transcription suite organized as a **Monorepo**. The codebase is split into surgical packages to enforce architectural boundaries:

| Package | Contains |
|------|----------|
| **Record-Foundation** | Domain types, Logging, and Infrastructure protocols. |
| **Record-Audio** | Audio capture I/O (Core Audio Taps, IOProc). |
| **Record-ML** | Local ML inference (WhisperKit, MLX, DuckDB storage). |
| **Record-Presentation** | SwiftUI views and Newspaper-style UI. |
| **Record-App** | Business layer (Use Case actors) and the Composition Root. |
| **Record-Pro** | Guided generation, transcript repair, and DER metrics. |

Dependencies flow inward: `Record-Foundation` is the base. `Record-App` orchestrates all other packages to build the final executable.

## This Repo's Role

This repository is the central hub for THE RECORD suite. It contains:
- **Core Source Code**: All Swift packages mentioned above.
- **Shared Tooling**: Scripts for building prebuilts, managing fixtures, and architectural analysis.
- **Architectural Guardrails**: Formal ADRs and Invariants that govern the suite's evolution.

## Development Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gitrdunhq/the-record-suite.git
cd the-record-suite
./onboarding.sh
```

The `onboarding.sh` script will fetch binary dependencies, download ML fixtures, and build your initial knowledge graphs.

### Requirements
- macOS 15.0+ (M1+ Apple Silicon required for ML)
- Xcode 16.2+
- Swift 6.2 (Strict Concurrency enabled)
- Python 3.10+

## Code Standards

### GRAPHIFY FIRST (Mandatory)
No PR or architectural change may proceed without an up-to-date knowledge graph. Run `./scripts/graphify_suite.sh` to refresh your maps before planning changes.

### TDD Discipline
We follow strict Test-Driven Development. Never write implementation code before a failing test.
1. **RED**: Write a failing test in the appropriate `Tests/` directory.
2. **GREEN**: Implement minimal logic to pass.
3. **REFACTOR**: Clean up while maintaining GREEN state.

### Actor Isolation
All shared mutable state must be isolated in Swift `actor` types. No `nonisolated(unsafe)` hatches allowed.

## PR Process

1. Create a feature branch.
2. Make surgical changes following TDD.
3. Verify the full 1500+ test suite passes: `swift test`.
4. Update the relevant `PROPERTIES.md` for your epic.
5. Open a PR with a clear description of the "Why."

## Human Onboarding

If you are new to the project, please read **`ONBOARDING.md`** for a deep dive into the environment setup and architectural patterns.

## License

Record-Suite is private software. Copyright 2026 gitrdunhq. All rights reserved.

content.content:
[see-something] bug: AppAssembler.storage never assigned, teardown DB close silently no-ops (AppAssembler.swift:39,67)
## What's wrong

\`AppAssembler\` declares \`var storage: GRDBStorageActor?\` (AppAssembler.swift:39), and \`teardown()\` calls \`try await storage?.close()\` (line 67) expecting this to close the DB pool on app shutdown.

But \`assemble()\` never assigns \`self.storage\`. It builds a local \`let st = await buildStorage()\` (line ~75 in the current version) and threads \`st\` through to every VM/use-case constructor — but never does \`self.storage = st\`. So the instance property stays \`nil\` for the app's entire lifetime, and \`storage?.close()\` in \`teardown()\` is a silent no-op.

## Why it matters

\`GRDBStorageActor.close()\` exists specifically to flush/checkpoint the WAL and close the SQLite connection pool cleanly. If it never actually runs, a force-quit or fast system shutdown has a higher chance of leaving the WAL in a state that needs recovery on next launch (and in the worst case, if the shutdown coincides with a checkpoint boundary, corruption). This is exactly the kind of resource-cleanup bug the async teardown refactor (#280) was meant to make foolproof — the plumbing works, but the assignment that would have populated it was dropped.

## Where I found it

Noticed while wiring #300 (speaker enrollment) — I added a *separate* \`Assembled.storage: GRDBStorageActor\` field (non-optional, returned from \`assemble()\`) to expose the storage actor to \`App.swift\` for the new Settings enrollment UI. That's unrelated to this bug; the pre-existing \`AppAssembler.storage\` instance property is the one that's dead.

## Suggested fix

In \`assemble()\`, right after \`let st = await buildStorage()\`, add \`self.storage = st\`. One line.

## User Story
As a user reviewing a transcript, I want to see which speaker said each part of the transcript, so I can follow multi-speaker conversations more easily.

TranscriptTabView displays raw transcript text without speaker attribution. Diarization speaker boundaries exist in a separate data stream and need to be merged with transcript segments for a unified speaker-labeled view.

- [ ] Edge cases handled: single speaker, unknown speaker, overlapping diarization
- [ ] Accessibility: speaker labels announced in VoiceOver

[see-something] correctness: smart auto-record consumer never wired — startAutoRecording() is dead code (RecordingStateViewModel.swift:156)
**What's wrong.** `RecordingStateViewModel.startAutoRecording(detector:onMeetingStarted:onMeetingStopped:isRecording:)` (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/ViewModels/RecordingStateViewModel.swift:156`) is a fully implemented consumer for `any MeetingDetector` event streams, but it is never called anywhere in the composition root (`AppAssembler`/`AppAssemblerBuilders`). Found while fixing #250 (CalendarAwareMeetingDetector never retained).

Even after #250's fix retains `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector` and lets it actually run, its `events()` stream still has no listener — nothing calls `startAutoRecording`. The bare `AudioSessionDetector` (also constructed in `buildMenuBarVM`) is in the same boat: its events aren't consumed by the auto-record path either.

Two additional disconnects compound this:
1. `Feature.smartAutoRecording` (`Record-Foundation/Sources/Domain/Licensing/Feature.swift:18`) is a gated "Standard" tier licensed feature, but there is no `FeatureGate` check anywhere near `RecordingStateViewModel`/`MenuBarViewModel`/`AppAssembler` that would gate calling `startAutoRecording`.
2. `SettingsViewModel.autoRecordEnabled` (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/ViewModels/SettingsViewModel.swift:83`), bound to the "Auto-detect meetings" toggle in `SettingsViewGeneralTab.swift:168`, is a completely disconnected boolean — `SettingsViewModel` is constructed fresh every time the SwiftUI `Settings` scene renders (`Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/App.swift`), with no observation bridge back into the long-lived `RecordingStateViewModel.autoRecordEnabled`/`startAutoRecording()`/`stopAutoRecording()`.

**Why it matters.** "Auto-detect meetings" is a user-facing, licensed feature that currently does nothing when toggled on — no error, no log, just silent inertness. A paying Standard-tier user flipping this switch gets no behavior change at all.

**Suggested fix.** This needs a small feature-completion pass, not just a wiring fix:
- Read the persisted auto-record setting into `AppConfig`/composition root at `assemble()` time (it doesn't appear to be persisted anywhere currently — check whether it should live in `AppConfig` like other settings).
- Gate the call with a `FeatureGate`/license check for `.smartAutoRecording`.
- Call `recordingStateVM.startAutoRecording(detector:, onMeetingStarted:, onMeetingStopped:, isRecording:)` at assembly time when the setting is on, using `calendarAwareMeetingDetector` (now retained per #250) as the detector, with `onMeetingStarted`/`onMeetingStopped` closures wired to `recordingStateVM.startRecording()`/`stopRecording()`.
- Bridge the SwiftUI `SettingsViewModel.autoRecordEnabled` toggle change back into the long-lived `RecordingStateViewModel`/`AppAssembler` (today `SettingsViewModel` is reconstructed per Settings-window open with no persistence-and-reload path back to the composition root for this specific field — check how other Settings fields like `notionEnabled` achieve this round-trip via `ConfigManager`/`IntegrationSettingsStore` and follow the same pattern).

Deliberately left out of scope for the #250 bug-fix packet per its instructions to avoid inventing new architecture in what was meant to be a narrow retention fix.

[see-something] dead-feature: DataEraser has no real production conformer (LiveDataEraser doesn't exist)
Escalated from #216's composition-root audit (DataEraser row).

## What's wrong

`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Views/SettingsViewDeleteAllSection.swift` explicitly injects a placeholder:

```swift
// Bridge: call site uses SettingsView.deleteAllDataSection; inject NoOpDataEraser until
// the composition root wires a real DataEraser.
DeleteAllDataSection(viewModel: viewModel, dataEraser: NoOpDataEraser())
```

with the delete button itself already `.disabled(true)` (line 49, comment: `GITHUB ENHANCEMENT: Implement LiveDataEraser to handle SQLite teardown`). No `LiveDataEraser` type exists anywhere in the codebase — only `NoOpDataEraser` (production placeholder) and `MockDataEraser`/`FailingDataEraser` (test doubles in `SettingsViewModelDeleteAllTests.swift`).

## Impact

"Delete All Data" in Settings is a known, intentionally-disabled placeholder — not a silent bug (the UI already gates it off), but it's an incomplete feature that #216's contract-audit correctly flagged as unwired. Confirming here so it's tracked as its own item rather than buried in a 9-protocol audit.

## Suggested fix

Implement `LiveDataEraser: DataEraser` (SQLite/DuckDB teardown per the existing TODO comment), wire it into `AppAssembler`, and re-enable the button. This is a real feature-completion task, not a mechanical wiring fix — not attempted in this pass.
----
[see-something] correctness: ProofHarnessWindows pipeline wired entirely to stub engines — output is fake (Stubs.swift)
## What's wrong

`Record-CrossPlatform-Foundation/Sources/Infrastructure/Stubs.swift` defines five stub engines in a production Infrastructure target:

- `ParakeetPlugin` — returns `"[Parakeet Stub Output]"`
- `WhisperKitPlugin` — returns `"[Whisper Stub Output]"`
- `MLXSummarizationPlugin` — returns `"Stub Summary"`
- `FluidDiarizationPlugin` — returns one fake `SPEAKER_00` segment
- `AudioFileLoader` — returns 1 second of silence regardless of input file

Their only consumer is `ProofHarnessWindows/PipelineRunner.swift`, which wires all five. So the Windows proof harness runs end-to-end but every stage produces canned fake output — timing numbers and "results" it reports prove nothing about the real pipeline.

## Why it matters

# THE RECORD — Presentation Layer

The Broadsheet newspaper UI for THE RECORD. SwiftUI views and @Observable ViewModels.

## Building

**The standalone `swift build` in this directory is currently broken and unsupported** —
19 Presentation source files import `Business`, which lives in the root monorepo package
(`Record-App/Sources/Business`) and is not declared (or stubbable) in this package's
manifest. See issue #313. Until Business is extracted into a shared package, build and
test from the monorepo root:

```bash
cd ..            # the-record-suite root
swift build --target Presentation
swift test --filter <SuiteName>
```

## Architecture

- `ViewModels/` — @MainActor @Observable classes that drive the UI
- `Views/` — SwiftUI views organized by feature
- `Views/Components/` — Reusable UI components

- Xcode 16.2+
- Swift 6.2 (strict concurrency)

[see-something] correctness: mic-cleaned WAV is pure digital silence in production — AEC/sink chain writes no signal (AECProcessorActor.swift, WAVCleanedAudioSink)
**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

Investigated in `82af454d` (branch `fix/mega-remediation-20260701`). Findings:

**Self-cancellation hypothesis confirmed via synthetic-signal tests** (`AECSilentOutputInvestigationTests.swift`):
- 440Hz mic sine + silent far-end reference → healthy output, tail RMS 0.05102.
- Same mic signal fed back as its own far-end reference → output collapses to tail RMS 0.00003 (~1700x drop) after Speex converges. This is correct AEC behavior given a self-referential far-end input, **not a bug in `AECProcessorActor`**.

**`RecordingStateViewModelStreaming.swift`'s far-end wiring checked (read-only) and found logically sound**: `systemAudioRingBuffer` is populated exclusively from the `.system` track stream, never from mic frames — no static aliasing bug at that layer.

**Added a diagnostic guard** (no behavior change to AEC itself): `AECProcessorActor` now logs once after ~800ms of sustained near-zero output despite non-silent mic input, so future occurrences are visible in logs instead of silent.

**Root cause not found** — if self-cancellation is really happening in the field, the far-end reference itself is likely wrong further upstream, at the system-audio capture/routing layer (`CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` / `StartRecordingUseCase.getSystemStream()`), which requires live-device investigation, not static reading. Filed as a follow-up issue rather than guessing at a fix here. Leaving this issue open until that's resolved.

Independently verified: full Record-Audio suite green, 177 tests / 29 suites.
**Scope narrowed after re-verification against current `main` (2026-07-04 agent-swarm triage).**

Done since filing:
- Log-once diagnostic guard shipped in `AECProcessorActor.swift:84-112` (commit 82af454d) — sustained silence-despite-signal now surfaces in production logs
- Self-cancellation hypothesis confirmed by `AECSilentOutputInvestigationTests.swift` — AEC math is correct given its inputs; feeding the mic's own signal as far-end collapses output to near-zero
- Sub-issues #190, #192, #231 closed

**This issue now tracks only the upstream investigation:** if self-cancellation is the real-world root cause, the garbage far-end reference originates in system audio capture/routing (likely `RecordingStateViewModelStreaming` / CoreAudio tap wiring), not in the AEC. Next step is correlating the new diagnostic logs from a live repro. Related: #248.

```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes

// CORRECT

```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

(actor re-entrancy, @unchecked Sendable, parallel test conflicts, diagnostic methodology).

These docs exist but don't read them unless working on that layer:

- `docs/planning/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md` (1239 lines)

Format: `Epic {N}: [{Layer}] {Description}`

```
Sources/Domain/          ← library: Foundation only
Sources/Business/        ← library: depends on Domain
Sources/Infrastructure/  ← library: depends on Domain + 3rd-party
Sources/Presentation/    ← library: depends on Domain + Business
```

This project is indexed by GitNexus as **the-record** (5454 symbols, 52742 relationships, 239 execution flows). Use the GitNexus MCP tools to understand code, assess impact, and navigate safely.

> If any GitNexus tool warns the index is stale, run `npx gitnexus analyze` in terminal first.

## Always Do

- **MUST run impact analysis before editing any symbol.** Before modifying a function, class, or method, run `gitnexus_impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})` and report the blast radius (direct callers, affected processes, risk level) to the user.
- **MUST run `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before committing** to verify your changes only affect expected symbols and execution flows.
- **MUST warn the user** if impact analysis returns HIGH or CRITICAL risk before proceeding with edits.
- When exploring unfamiliar code, use `gitnexus_query({query: "concept"})` to find execution flows instead of grepping. It returns process-grouped results ranked by relevance.
- When you need full context on a specific symbol — callers, callees, which execution flows it participates in — use `gitnexus_context({name: "symbolName"})`.

## Never Do

- NEVER edit a function, class, or method without first running `gitnexus_impact` on it.
- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis.
- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `gitnexus_rename` which understands the call graph.
- NEVER commit changes without running `gitnexus_detect_changes()` to check affected scope.

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

## Finding

`HardwareBoundaryProfiler` and `SystemHardwarePoller` interact directly with IOKit and system hardware APIs (e.g., `os_log_create`, hardware telemetry). These are infrastructure-tier components, yet they are currently placed in `Record-Foundation/Sources/Utilities/` — which is Domain-tier, adjacent to business logic.

## Location

- `/Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/the-record-suite/Record-Foundation/Sources/Utilities/HardwareBoundaryProfiler.swift`
- `/Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/the-record-suite/Record-Foundation/Sources/Utilities/SystemHardwarePoller.swift`

## Why It Matters

Layer separation is a hard constraint in THE RECORD architecture:
- **Presentation** → **Business** → **Domain** → **Foundation** (allowed only)
- **Foundation** ↛ **Infrastructure** (Foundation should not depend on concrete I/O)

Hardware polling is infrastructure. Placing it in Foundation violates this contract and makes it difficult to swap implementations (e.g., for testing or alternative telemetry backends).

## Suggested Fix

Move both files to `Record-Infrastructure/Sources/` (or a new `Record-Telemetry/Sources/` if hardware metrics are significant enough to warrant a dedicated package). Update imports in Record-ML and any other consumers.

content.content:
## User Story

As a performance engineer, I want to profile WhisperKitPlugin and FluidDiarizationPlugin using Instruments.app so that I can identify bottlenecks in model loading, warm-up, and inference and optimize hot paths.

## Context

THE RECORD's inference plugins (WhisperKitPlugin for ASR, FluidDiarizationPlugin for speaker diarization) have multiple stages: model load, warm-up, per-chunk inference. These are ideal candidates for profiling. Using `os.signpost` intervals, we can visualize these stages in Instruments.app under a custom instrument.

This requires adding `OSSignpost` logging to key code paths with consistent subsystem (`com.therecord.app`) and category (`Performance`).

## Acceptance Criteria

### WhisperKitPlugin

- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval: `loadModel` — from start of model initialization to ready
- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval: `warmupModels` — from start of prewarm to completion
- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval per chunk: `transcribeChunk` — from API call entry to result return (include chunk ID)
- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval for full job: `transcriptionJob` — from first chunk to last chunk (duration of entire job)
- [ ] Emit subsystem: `com.therecord.app`, category: `Performance`

### FluidDiarizationPlugin

- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval: `loadModel` — from init to ready
- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval per segment: `diarizeSegment` — from segment processing to speaker label assigned
- [ ] Add OSSignpost interval for full job: `diarizationJob` — from first segment to last (duration of entire diarization)
- [ ] Same subsystem/category as WhisperKit

13	/// Wraps OSSignposter with SystemHardwarePoller to capture CPU and GPU metrics
14	/// at strategic execution boundaries.
15	public actor HardwareBoundaryProfiler {
16	    private let poller: SystemHardwarePollerProtocol
17	    private let signposter: OSSignposter
18	    /// Injected by callers that have MLX access so GPU peak memory is real.
19	    /// Defaults to 0 (placeholder) when called from layers without MLX.
20	    private let mlxPeakProvider: @Sendable () -> Int64
21	
22	    public init(
23	        category: String,
24	        poller: SystemHardwarePollerProtocol = SystemHardwarePoller(),
25	        mlxPeakProvider: @escaping @Sendable () -> Int64 = { 0 }
26	    ) {
27	        self.poller = poller
28	        self.signposter = AppLogger.signposter(category: category)
29	        self.mlxPeakProvider = mlxPeakProvider
30	    }
31	
32	    /// Begins a profiling interval, capturing initial hardware state.
33	    public func begin(_ name: StaticString) async -> BoundaryToken {
34	        let state = signposter.beginInterval(name, id: signposter.makeSignpostID())
35	        let snapshot = await poller.captureProcessSnapshot()
36	        return BoundaryToken(state: state, startSnapshot: snapshot, name: name)
37	    }
38	
39	    /// Ends a profiling interval, calculating hardware deltas and emitting the signpost.
40	    public func end(_ token: BoundaryToken) async {
41	        let endSnapshot = await poller.captureProcessSnapshot()
42	        let mlxMemory = mlxPeakProvider()
43	
44	        if let start = token.startSnapshot, let end = endSnapshot {
45	            let cpuUtil = await poller.calculateCpuUtilization(from: start.cpu, to: end.cpu)
46	            let memDiff = end.memoryMB - start.memoryMB
47	            let cpuPercent = cpuUtil * 100.0
48	            
49	            let msg = "CPU Util: \(String(format: "%.1f", cpuPercent))% | Mem Δ: \(memDiff) MB | GPU Peak: \(mlxMemory) bytes"
50	            print("[TELEMETRY] \(token.name) => \(msg)")
51	            signposter.endInterval(
52	                token.name,
53	                token.state,
54	                "CPU Util: \(cpuPercent, format: .fixed(precision: 1))% | Mem Δ: \(memDiff) MB | GPU Peak: \(mlxMemory) bytes"
55	            )
56	        } else {
57	            signposter.endInterval(token.name, token.state)
58	        }
59	    }
60	
61	    /// Emits a point-in-time snapshot event without an interval.
62	    public func emitSnapshotEvent(_ name: StaticString) async {
63	        guard let snap = await poller.captureProcessSnapshot() else { return }
64	        let mlxMemory = mlxPeakProvider()
65	        let msg = "CPU Ticks: \(snap.cpu.user + snap.cpu.system) | Mem: \(snap.memoryMB) MB | GPU: \(mlxMemory) bytes"
66	        print("[TELEMETRY-SNAPSHOT] \(name) => \(msg)")
67	        signposter.emitEvent(
68	            name,

70	        )

11	// →modelNotLoaded, all inference errors→inferenceFailed, TimeoutError→timeout(300).

13	/// ANE-optimised WhisperKit transcription engine.
14	///
15	/// ## ANE Strategy (Granola pattern)
16	/// Encoder runs on Apple Neural Engine for heavy matrix operations (~3x speedup).
17	/// Decoder runs on CPU for lightweight token generation (lower power draw).
18	///
19	/// ## Thread Safety
20	/// All mutable state (`whisperKit`, `loadedModelId`, `sequenceCounter`) is
21	/// actor-isolated. No unchecked-Sendable workaround is required.
22	///
23	/// `WhisperKit` is a non-Sendable class and never crosses isolation boundaries.
24	/// The `withTimeout` closure captures `self` (this actor, which IS `Sendable`)
25	/// and calls the actor-isolated `runTranscription(samples:)` helper. That method
26	/// accesses `whisperKit` entirely on the actor's executor so the non-Sendable
27	/// reference stays within a single isolation domain at all times.
28	public actor WhisperKitPlugin: TranscriptionEngine {
29	    // MARK: - Intermediate DTO
30	
31	    ///
32	    /// `WhisperKit.TranscriptionSegment` cannot be named via `WhisperKit.<Type>`
33	    /// because the compiler resolves the `WhisperKit.` qualifier to the class, not
34	    /// the module. This private struct captures only the fields that `buildSegment`
35	    /// needs (text, start, end, avgLogprob), all of which are primitive types that
36	    /// cross the actor isolation boundary safely.
37	    struct ExtractedSegment {
38	        let text: String
39	        let start: Float
40	        let end: Float
41	        let avgLogprob: Float
42	    }
43	
44	    // MARK: - Actor State
45	
46	    private var whisperKit: WhisperKit?
47	    private var loadedModelId: ModelID?
48	    private var sequenceCounter = 0
49	    private var lastComputeUnit: ComputeUnit = .unknown
50	    public private(set) var downloadDelegate: (any ModelDownloadDelegate)?
51	
52	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "WhisperKit")
53	
54	    // MARK: - Init
55	
56	    public init() {}
57	
58	    public func setDownloadDelegate(_ delegate: (any ModelDownloadDelegate)?) {
59	        downloadDelegate = delegate
60	    }
61	
62	    // MARK: - TranscriptionEngine
63	
64	    public func loadModel(_ modelId: ModelID) async throws {
65	        // Idempotent: skip if the same model is already loaded and ready.
66	        if loadedModelId == modelId, whisperKit != nil {
67	            logger.info("Model '\(modelId, privacy: .public)' already loaded — skipping")
68	            return
69	        }
70	
71	        logger.info("Loading WhisperKit model '\(modelId, privacy: .public)'")
72	        await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(.init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 0.0, phase: .downloading))
73	
74	        // ANE-first: encoder on ANE (heavy matrix ops), decoder on CPU (lightweight).
75	        let computeOptions = ModelComputeOptions(
76	            melCompute: .cpuAndGPU,
77	            audioEncoderCompute: .cpuAndNeuralEngine,
78	            textDecoderCompute: .cpuOnly
79	        )
80	        lastComputeUnit = .cpuAndNeuralEngine
81	
82	        do {
83	            // Respect cancellation before starting the download (e.g. if a caller wraps
84	            // loadModel in withTimeout and the deadline fires before we begin).
85	            try Task.checkCancellation()
86	            let kit = try await WhisperKit(
87	                model: modelId.rawValue,
88	                computeOptions: computeOptions,
89	                verbose: false,
90	                logLevel: .none,
91	                prewarm: false,
92	                load: true,
93	                download: true
94	            )
95	            whisperKit = kit
96	            loadedModelId = modelId
97	            await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(.init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 0.8, phase: .compiling))
98	            logger.info("WhisperKit model '\(modelId, privacy: .public)' loaded")
99	            // warmUp() translates its own errors into TranscriptionError.
100	            // Catch TranscriptionError first to avoid double-wrapping in the
101	            // WhisperError handler below.
102	            try await warmUp()
103	            await downloadDelegate?.downloadProgress(.init(modelId: modelId, fractionCompleted: 1.0, phase: .ready))
104	        } catch let error as TranscriptionError {
105	            whisperKit = nil
106	            loadedModelId = nil
107	            throw error
108	        } catch let error as WhisperError {
109	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
110	            logger.error("Load error: \(errDesc, privacy: .private)")
111	            whisperKit = nil
112	            loadedModelId = nil
113	            throw mapLoadError(error)
114	        } catch let error as ArgmaxCoreError {
115	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
116	            logger.error("Load error: \(errDesc, privacy: .private)")
117	            whisperKit = nil
118	            loadedModelId = nil
119	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: error)
120	        } catch {
121	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
122	            logger.error("Load error: \(errDesc, privacy: .private)")
123	            whisperKit = nil
124	            loadedModelId = nil
125	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: error)
126	        }
127	    }

129	    public func transcribe(
130	        samples: [Float],
131	        context: TranscriptionContext
132	    ) async throws -> Domain.TranscriptionSegment {
133	        guard !samples.isEmpty else { throw TranscriptionError.audioTooShort }
134	        guard whisperKit != nil else { throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: nil) }
135	        logger.debug(
136	            // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
137	            "Transcribing \(samples.count, privacy: .public) samples | session: \(context.sessionId?.rawValue ?? "none", privacy: .private)"
138	        )
139	        let rawData = try await fetchRawData(samples: samples)
140	        let seqNum = sequenceCounter
141	        sequenceCounter += 1
142	        return buildSegment(
143	            segments: rawData.segments,
144	            fallbackText: rawData.fallbackText,
145	            context: context,
146	            sequenceNumber: seqNum
147	        )
148	    }

150	    /// Returns one ``TranscriptionSegment`` per WhisperKit chunk so that
151	    /// downstream diarization can align speaker boundaries with fine-grained
152	    /// timestamps instead of a single blob spanning the whole recording.
153	    public func transcribeSegments(
154	        samples: [Float],
155	        context: TranscriptionContext
156	    ) async throws -> [Domain.TranscriptionSegment] {
157	        guard !samples.isEmpty else { throw TranscriptionError.audioTooShort }
158	        guard whisperKit != nil else { throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: nil) }
159	        let rawData = try await fetchRawData(samples: samples)
160	        guard !rawData.segments.isEmpty else {
161	            let seqNum = sequenceCounter
162	            sequenceCounter += 1
163	            return [buildSegment(
164	                segments: [],
165	                fallbackText: rawData.fallbackText,
166	                context: context,
167	                sequenceNumber: seqNum
168	            )]
169	        }
170	        // Safe: .map executes synchronously after the await returns — no reentrancy gap on sequenceCounter.
171	        return rawData.segments.map { extracted in
172	            let seqNum = sequenceCounter
173	            sequenceCounter += 1
174	            return buildSingleSegment(extracted, context: context, sequenceNumber: seqNum)
175	        }
176	    }
177	
178	    public func unloadModel() async {
179	        whisperKit = nil
180	        loadedModelId = nil
181	        logger.info("WhisperKit model unloaded")
182	    }
183	
184	    public func isReady() async -> Bool {
185	        whisperKit != nil
186	    }
187	
188	    public func getComputeUnit() async -> ComputeUnit {
189	        lastComputeUnit
190	    }
191	
192	    public func warmUp() async throws(TranscriptionError) {
193	        guard let kit = whisperKit else {
194	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: nil)
195	        }
196	        logger.info("Running ANE warm-up pass (CoreML model compilation)")
197	        do {
198	            try await kit.prewarmModels()
199	            logger.info("ANE warm-up complete")
200	        } catch let error as WhisperError {
201	            if case .initializationError = error {
202	                throw TranscriptionError.aneCompilationFailed
203	            }
204	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: error)
205	        } catch {
206	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: error)
207	        }
208	    }
209	
210	    // MARK: - Private Inference Helpers
211	
212	    /// Shared timeout + error-mapping wrapper used by both `transcribe` and
213	    /// `transcribeSegments`. Keeps the 300 s budget and WhisperError translation in
214	    /// one place so they can't drift apart.
215	    func fetchRawData(
216	        samples: [Float]
217	    ) async throws -> (segments: [ExtractedSegment], fallbackText: String) {
218	        do {
219	            return try await withTimeout(TimeoutConfig.whisperKitInference) {
220	                try await self.runTranscription(samples: samples)
221	            }
222	        } catch is TimeoutError {
223	            let tc = TimeoutConfig.whisperKitInference.components
224	            throw TranscriptionError.timeout(duration: TimeInterval(tc.seconds) + TimeInterval(tc.attoseconds) * 1e-18)
225	        } catch is CancellationError {
226	            throw CancellationError()
227	        } catch let error as WhisperError {
228	            throw mapInferenceError(error)
229	        } catch let error as TranscriptionError {
230	            throw error
231	        } catch {
232	            throw TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
233	        }
234	    }
235	
236	    /// Calls WhisperKit's `transcribe` within actor isolation.
237	    ///
238	    /// `WhisperKit` is a non-Sendable class. Confining all access to this
239	    /// actor-isolated method keeps the reference within a single isolation domain.
240	    func runTranscription(
241	        samples: [Float]
242	    ) async throws -> (segments: [ExtractedSegment], fallbackText: String) {
243	        guard let kit = whisperKit else {
244	            throw TranscriptionError.modelNotLoaded(underlying: nil)
245	        }
246	
247	        try Task.checkCancellation()
248	
249	        let results = try await kit.transcribe(
250	            audioArray: samples,
251	            decodeOptions: nil,
252	            callback: { _ in
253	                if Task.isCancelled {
254	                    return false
255	                }
256	                return true
257	            }
258	        )
259	
260	        try Task.checkCancellation()
261	
262	        let segments = results.flatMap { result in
263	            result.segments.map { seg in
264	                ExtractedSegment(
265	                    text: Self.stripTimestampTokens(seg.text),
266	                    start: seg.start,
267	                    end: seg.end,
268	                    avgLogprob: seg.avgLogprob
269	                )
270	            }
271	        }
272	        let fallbackText = results.map { Self.stripTimestampTokens($0.text) }.joined(separator: " ")
273	        return (segments, fallbackText)
274	    }
275	}

7	/// Tuning for the offline (batch) VBx diarization pipeline.
8	///

10	/// ProofHarness sweeps (2026-07): pure AHC→VBx with no speaker-count bounds
11	/// is deterministic (bounds trigger FluidAudio's KMeans fallback, which is
12	/// initialization-sensitive), the AHC threshold sits mid-plateau, and a
13	/// centroid-merge second pass repairs over-clustering without a count prior.
14	///
15	/// Measured against RTTM ground truth (no collar):
16	/// meeting-15min 85.1% purity / 28.2% DER (oracle ceiling 87.5% / 26.2%),
17	/// AMI ES2004a 83.3% / 24.2% (oracle 83.7% / 23.8%). Shipped streaming
18	/// engine on the same fixture: 78.0% / 35.8%.
19	public struct OfflineDiarizationTuning: Sendable, Equatable {
20	    /// AHC threshold. On these fixtures higher → more clusters; 0.8–0.9 is a
21	    /// stable plateau on both synthetic and AMI fixtures.
22	    public var clusteringThreshold: Double
23	
24	    /// Segmentation window hop as a fraction of window length. 0.1 matches
25	    /// pyannote reference accuracy; FluidAudio's 0.2 default trades ~1.4%
26	    /// DER for speed.

30	    /// post-processing recipe value.

34	    /// duplicate clusters of one speaker; 0.5 is too aggressive (merges
